name: application-symptom-severity-slider
title: Symptom Severity Slider
description: Native 0-10 range slider for self-reported pain/symptom severity, with a live numeric readout and a derived descriptor label (None/Mild/Moderate/Severe).
useWhen: Collecting a self-reported severity or pain rating on the standard clinical 0-10 scale.
You want both a precise number and a qualitative descriptor (Mild/Moderate/Severe) to reduce ambiguity for the person reporting.
The color gradient from green to red helps convey escalating severity at a glance.
avoidWhen: The scale isn't 0-10 or doesn't map to standard severity descriptors — use range-inputs directly with your own labeling.
You need discrete named options rather than a continuous slider — use radio-groups or a segmented control instead.
Color-coded severity could be misread as a diagnosis or clinical judgment rather than a patient-reported value — pair with clear copy clarifying it's self-reported.
responsiveBehavior: The slider is a fixed max-w-sm block that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: Built on a native <input type="range">, which provides built-in keyboard support (arrow keys) without extra ARIA.
The current value and descriptor are always shown as visible text, not conveyed by thumb position or color alone.
Endpoint and midpoint labels (0 · None, 5 · Moderate, 10 · Worst) anchor the scale so its meaning doesn't depend on memorizing a legend.
